relationships.statement: The double-slit experiment produces an interference pattern.
The Standard Model is a quantum field theory.
The correspondence principle constrains quantum theory to converge to classical limits.

claims.statement: The Rydberg formula predicted the absorption lines of hydrogen gas using a constant and integers indexing the lines.
Wave–particle duality states that neither the classical concept of a particle nor that of a wave fully describes photons or matter.
Variations of the double-slit experiment using electrons, atoms, and large molecules produce the same type of interference pattern.
An object with a definite value for a property is said to possess an eigenstate.
Quantum mechanics studies matter and its interactions with energy at atomic and subatomic scales.
Classical physics could not explain some phenomena, and this contributed to the development of quantum mechanics through a revolution in physics.
Wave function collapse converts a probabilistic or potential quantum state into a definite measured value.
Quantum mechanics explains how atoms interact with each other and form molecules.
The Stern–Gerlach experiment showed that a beam of atoms separates into two streams in a magnetic field rather than a continuous range of directions.
The uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of physical properties cannot be simultaneously measured or defined to arbitrary precision.
Superfluidity is a phenomenon in which liquid helium near absolute zero spontaneously flows up and over its container rim, an effect classical physics cannot explain.
Quantum entanglement occurs when the quantum state of each particle in a group cannot be described independently of the others, even when they are widely separated.
Planck used discrete energy entities to explain black-body radiation.
Quantum tunneling is vital to a simple light switch because electrons in the electric current must penetrate an oxide potential barrier.
In the photoelectric effect, the number of emitted electrons depends on light intensity, while their velocity does not depend on intensity.
The Dirac wave equation incorporated relativity, predicted antimatter, and provided a complete theory for the Stern–Gerlach result.
Quantum field theory allows the creation and annihilation of particles.
The Pauli exclusion principle states that two electrons within an atom cannot have the same set of quantum numbers.
Applications of quantum mechanics include lasers, transistors, electron microscopes, and magnetic resonance imaging.
Quantum electrodynamics is the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force.
Einstein proposed that light consists of energy quanta rather than being only a continuous wave.
